Retrying...\" | automatic retry |\n1026\t| `E-MANIFEST-LIVELOCK` | E12 livelock detected, manifest corrupted (bf-5fm) | \"Multiple chunks failed verification — the manifest appears corrupted. Re-decoding manifest...\" | re-decode manifest |\n1027\t| `E-BLOCK-HASH` | Rank K reached, hash failed (E12) | \"A chunk arrived corrupted and is being re-collected.\" | automatic retry |\n1028\t| `E-BLOCK-RETRY-EXCEEDED` | Block retry limit exceeded (E12 livelock, bf-5fm) | \"A chunk has failed verification too many times. Re-decoding manifest...\" | re-decode manifest |\n1029\t| `E-K-OVERFLOW` | Sender K exceeds receiver's maximum (D26) | \"Sender's chunk size is too large for this device. Use a smaller file or a more powerful receiver.\" | refuse, user adjusts |\n1030\t| `E-REPAIR-BOUNDS` | Repair code references blocks beyond file (§8.2) | \"That repair code refers to chunks that don't exist. Check it and try again.\" | user re-enters |\n1031\t| `E-REPAIR-CODE` | Repair code checksum failed | \"That repair code doesn't look right — check it and try again.\" | user re-enters |\n1032\t| `E-FILE-HASH` | Whole-file hash failed (E13) | \"The file is complete but failed its final check — saved as unverified.\" | keep output, warn |\n1033\t| `E-WASM-LOAD` | Decoder failed to load | \"The scanner failed to start. Reload the page.\" | user reloads |\n1034\t\n1035\t**Status codes** (informational, not errors):\n1036\t\n1037\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing |\n1038\t|---|---|---|\n1039\t| `E-VERIFYING` | Verifying blocks against manifest (§7.6) | \"Verifying received chunks against manifest...\" |\n1040\t\n1041\t**Local / resource:**\n1042\t\n1043\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing | Recovery |\n1044\t|---|---|---|---|\n1045\t| `E-QUOTA-PREFLIGHT` | Not enough storage (§13.1) | \"Not enough free space: this needs X, you have Y.\" | user frees space |\n1046\t| `E-QUOTA-EXHAUSTED` | Ran out mid-transfer (E10) | \"Out of space. Saved what arrived — X of Y chunks.\" | partial export |\n1047\t| `E-SOURCE-CHANGED` | Source mutated (E5) | \"The file changed while sending. Start again to avoid a corrupt copy.\" | restart required |\n1048\t| `E-BACKGROUNDED` | Sender tab backgrounded (E8) | \"Sending paused — keep this tab visible.\" | auto-resume on focus |\n1049\t| `E-CAMERA-LOST` | Permission revoked (E9) | \"Camera access ended. Your progress is saved.\" | re-grant, resume |\n1050\t| `E-WAKELOCK-LOST` | Screen may sleep | \"The screen may turn off. Adjust your sleep settings.\" | user acts |\n1051\t| `E-DECOMPRESS` | Decompression failed (E15) | \"Everything arrived but couldn't be unpacked. The raw data was kept.\" | keep artefact |\n1052\t\n1053\t---\n1054\t\n1055\t## 12. Threat model\n1056\t\n1057\tThe README claims \"provably no exfiltration\" and \"auditable once and trusted thereafter\".\n1058\tThat claim needs backing. In scope for v1:\n1059\t\n1060\t| # | Threat | Stance | Test |\n1061\t|---|---|---|---|\n1062\t| **T1** | **Crafted optical stream — resource exhaustion.** Beacon-declared `originalSize` and `payloadLen` (281 TB each), `blockCount` (16.7 M) and `L` are attacker-controlled and size allocations. | **Mitigated.** Bounds-check every beacon field before use: `L` ∈ [1, 4096], `K` ≤ locally benchmarked max (D26), `blockCount` ≤ 16.7 M, `originalSize` ≤ available quota, `payloadLen` ≤ available quota. Reject with `E-META-BOUNDS`. Never allocate from a declared size. | A10 + fuzz beacon fields |\n1063\t| **T2** | **Path traversal / hostile filename.** `filename` is attacker-supplied and reaches a save dialog. | **Mitigated.** Strip path separators, control bytes and leading dots; cap length; never pass through unsanitised. | unit: filenames with `../`, NUL, control bytes |\n1064\t| **T3** | **Decompression bomb.** The receiver decompresses attacker-supplied data. | **Mitigated.** Enforce a max expansion ratio (100:1) and an absolute cap = declared `originalSize`; abort with `E-DECOMPRESS` on overrun. | unit: 1 GB-expanding zip bomb → `E-DECOMPRESS` |\n1065\t| **T4a** | **Sender-side plaintext residue.** D8 writes a *decompressed-equivalent* copy of the user's file to OPFS as staging. For the flagship use case (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds) this is real exposure. | **Mitigated.** Wipe staging on completion, on cancel, and on startup-reap (E11). Document that OPFS is not encrypted at rest and the OS/browser may retain it. | integration: assert sender OPFS empty after complete/cancel/reap |\n1066\t| **T4b** | **Receiver-side plaintext residue.** The receiver stages the complete decoded file in OPFS. Risk register\n1390\t\n1391\t| # | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Trigger → fallback |\n1392\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n1393\t| **R1** | **GE still too slow at K=768 on real phones** | ~~Medium~~ **Low** | High — blocks Phase 1 | Cost model + conservative K (D19/D26). **S1 measured 3,260 MB/s desktop = 7.1× margin at Stage 3 after a ÷4 phone factor; provisionally closed pending an on-device re-run** | Measured need > budget → drop to K=512 (2.88× margin), then re-open D5 against wirehair/RaptorQ (whose linear-time decode is what libcimbar uses) |\n1394\t| **R2** | **4 camera px/module cliff makes handheld use impractical** | Medium | High | **Sender shapes the code region to the receiver's portrait aspect by default (§6.3.2) — clears the cliff without any user action.** Aim reticle + coach (`bf-1g0`), ladder (D16) as secondary aids | A2 fails → mandate a stand in the UI and reposition as a mounted-device tool |\n1395\t| **R3** | **Stage 1 measures far below 20 KB/s** | Medium | High — undermines the multi-GB objective | Tiling (D1) is the measured 10× | < 10 KB/s → cap the advertised file size, move Stage 2 earlier |\n1396\t| **R4** | **Phone→phone unusable at 54 cells** | **High** | Medium | Separate profile with bigger modules | A3 fails → document phone→phone as a small-file-only mode |\n1397\t| **R5** | **iOS cannot export multi-GB** | **High** | Medium | Detect and cap up front | `share()` fails > 1 GB → iOS is receive-capped, stated at file selection |\n1398\t| **R6** | **OPFS quota smaller than advertised** | Medium | Medium | Pre-flight (`bf-4d6`) + graceful stop (E10) | Repeated E-QUOTA-EXHAUSTED → lower the refuse threshold |\n1399\t| **R7** | **libcimbar MPL-2.0 contaminates the licence** | Low | Medium | Decide before Phase 7 (§19 Q1) | Cannot accept mixed licence → clean-room Stage 3 or stop at Stage 2 |\n1400\t| **R8** | **No way to learn real-world performance** (no telemetry by design) | **High** | Low | Accepted; promote the repair code (§8.2). Note v1 cannot *observe* erasure (D18a), so this is an assumption, not a controlled quantity | Erasure > 35% under §13.2 conditions → the **repair code becomes the primary recovery path, not the tail**, and dwell is re-derived from the measured band |\n1404\t| **R11** | **Thermal throttling makes long transfers self-defeating** | **High** (observed first session) | **High** — attacks the multi-GB objective directly | Duty-cycling (D27), decode-resolution drop, resume (D22). Self-reinforcing loop: SoC slows → decode slower → camera fps falls → erasure rises → transfer lengthens → more heat | **Trigger:** Discriminate sender-side (camera fps drops >30%, decode latency within +30%) vs receiver-side (decode latency increases >50%, camera fps within -20%) throttling per `docs/notes/bf-3mnt-thermal-throttling-discrimination.md`. Apply D27 duty-cycling only for receiver-side throttling. Sender-side throttling should NOT trigger receiver duty-cycling — doing so makes transfers slower without addressing the root cause. If duty-cycling cannot hold the rate, reframe multi-GB as a multi-session workflow (§1.1) |\n1405\t\n1406\t---\n1407\t\n1408\t## 18.1 Anti-patterns — mistakes this project has already made\n1409\t\n1410\tEvery entry below was made *in this repo* and cost real time. They are collected here because\n1411\teach was previously buried in the narrative of the section that fixed it, where an implementer\n1412\tstarting a later phase would never encounter it.\n1413\t\n1414\t| # | Anti-pattern | What it looked like | Guard |\n1415\t|---|---|---|---|\n1416\t| **AP1** | **A unit-free \"px/module\"** | Every optical run sat at 2.25 camera px/module while the config said \"4\". Presented as a symbology limit; was a sampling limit. | §2 defines screen px and camera px. Never write \"px/module\" unqualified. |\n1417\t| **AP2** | **The ROI ratchet** | A frame where only two tiles decoded shrank the crop to those two; every later frame then saw only that region and could never recover. Erasure 91%, goodput **worse than no cropping**, and it presents as an *optical* fault. | Wide margin (≥35%) **plus a forced full-frame rescan every N frames**. An ROI that can only shrink is a bug. |\n1418\t| **AP3** | **Sizing K from GE's memory term** | K = 16,384 gave a 32 MB matrix (fine) and needed 4.5 GB/s of XOR (23× over). | K is bound by *time*, not memory (§3.1). Faster wire rate makes decode **harder**. |\n1419\t| **AP4** | **Setting L from the nominal ladder rung** | L = 507 made the conservative rung carry **zero** packets, destroying the ladder's only guarantee. | L is set by the **smallest** rung (§3.1.1); `params.ts` throws at import if a rung cannot hold a whole packet. |\n1420\t| **AP5** | **Running the sender faster than D9 allows** | 2.8× over the half-camera-fps rule → 78% erasure. Looked like poor optics. | D9 is a constraint to satisfy, not a dial to maximise. |\n1421\t| **AP6** | **Narrowing the erasure band instead of raising dwell** | Contradicted the evidence base and cost throughput for no arithmetic reason. | Raise dwell; the band is an assumption about the channel (D18c), not a target. |\n1422\t| **AP7** | **Trusting `getSettings()` / requested capture** | Reports 30/60 fps while delivering 15; defaults to 1080 on the *short* edge. | Measure delivered fps and actual capture dimensions (D14, §6.4). |\n1423\t| **AP8** | **`--use-fake-device-for-media-capture`** | Does not exist. It is `--use-fake-device-for-media-**stream**`. | §14.1. |\n1424\t| **AP9** | **Never offering a torch button** | 3.6× fps gain makes it tempting; an LED on glossy glass destroys a region of the frame. | §6.4. |\n1425\t| **AP10** | **Writing a comment that asserts a file exists** | `prng.ts` claimed `test/fixtures/vectors.json` pinned the wire format. It did not exist. | Generate the artifact in the same commit as the claim (§14.3). |\n1426\t\n1427\t## 18.2 Proof obligations\n1428\t\n1429\tEach load-bearing assumption, what must be true, and what would invalidate it. This exists\n1430\tbecause the project has a documented history of confident-and-wrong (AP1, AP3, AP4, plus a\n1431\t2× formula error), and G7 only makes *one* class of claim executable.\n1432\t\n1433\t| Assumption | Holds iff | Invalidating evidence | Fallback |\n1434\t|---|---|---|---|\n1435\t| D19's K = 768 | phone GE ≥ 114.6 MB/s sustained **while thermally throttled** | on-device benchmark under load | K → 512 (2.88× margin), then re-open D5 vs wirehair (R1) |\n1436\t| S1's ÷4 phone factor | desktop-to-phone JS gap ≤ 4× | on-device `ge-bench.mjs` | recompute K from the measured figure |\n1437\t| D18c's 20–30% erasure | erasure under §13.2 conditions stays ≤ 30% | measured 48% (non-qualifying conditions) | repair code (§8.2) becomes the primary path, not the tail (R12) |\n1438\t| The 4 camera px/module cliff | zxing needs ≥ 4 camera px/module under handheld blur | S3 distance sweep under §13.2 conditions | re-derive the rung ladder from the measured cliff |\n1439\t| D1's ~10× tiling gain | holds on hardware, not just simulated camera paths | rung sweep on the rig | drop to fewer, larger tiles |\n1440\t| D27's duty-cycle economics | 50% duty ≈ 50% heat and completes | long-run thermal profile | multi-session framing (§1.1), or cap the supported file size |\n1441\t| Stage 3's value | decode CPU/bit beats QR's | prototype against a worker-pool QR baseline | stay at Stage 2 |\n1442\t\n1443\t## 19. A full-bleed high-contrast animation at 12–15 fps for\n1493\thours is a genuine seizure risk.\n1494\t\n1495\t**The mitigation costs the core metric.** Bounding flash area reduces usable screen area →\n1496\tfewer cells → less throughput. Two ways out:\n1508\t\n1509\t1. **Scope delta as a v2 mode with its own block scheme** — cleanest; the fixed-block path\n1510\t   stays untouched.\n1511\t2. **Keep fixed blocks and diff at block granularity** — no rolling hash, but only detects\n1512\t   changes aligned to 192 KB boundaries, so an insertion near the start re-sends\n1513\t   everything after it.\n1514\t\n1515\tOption 2 is dramatically cheaper and probably sufficient for the air-gapped-update case,\n1516\twhere changes are usually appends or whole-component replacements. **Start there.** The\n1517\tnear-term half — robust cross-session resume — has no such tension and ships first.\n1518\t\n1519\t---\n1520\t\n1521\t## 21. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_7e071991def4402a865ab9fe","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# screenferry\n2\t\n3\t**Move a file between two devices using nothing but a screen and a camera.**\n4\t\n5\tscreenferry is a static web app — no server, no backend, no network between the two\n6\tdevices. The sending device reads a local file and flashes it out as an animated\n7\tsequence of optical codes. The receiving device runs the *same* web app, points\n8\tits camera at the sender's screen, decodes the frames, and reassembles the\n9\toriginal file byte-for-byte.\n10\t\n11\t```\n12\t┌─────────────────┐                      ┌─────────────────┐\n13\t│    SENDER       │   ░▓█ optical ░▓█    │    RECEIVER     │\n14\t│                 │  ──────────────────► │                 │\n15\t│  file → chunks  │  animated code frames│  frames → file  │\n16\t│  → coded frames │   screen to camera   │  → download     │\n17\t└─────────────────┘                      └─────────────────┘\n18\t        same static web app on both ends\n19\t```\n20\t\n21\tAnimated QR codes are the obvious way to do this, and the likely starting point —\n22\tbut the goal is the *channel*, not the format. QR spends most of its capacity on\n23\trobustness screenferry doesn't need (arbitrary angles, print damage, one bit per\n24\tmodule). Denser modulation — colored cells, stacked RGB codes, a purpose-built\n25\tgrid codec — is on the table wherever it survives a real phone camera. The\n26\tarchitecture keeps that layer swappable.\n27\t\n28\t## Why\n29\t\n30\tThe screen-to-camera channel is the one data path that survives when everything\n31\telse is unavailable or untrusted:\n32\t\n33\t- **Air-gapped systems** — the receiving machine is deliberately not on any network.\n34\t- **Hostile or captive networks** — hotel wifi, conference NAT, corporate DLP.\n35\t- **Cross-ecosystem transfer** — AirDrop doesn't talk to Android; Nearby Share doesn't talk to iOS.\n36\t- **No pairing, no accounts, no cloud** — nothing is uploaded anywhere, because\n37\t  there is nowhere to upload it to. The bytes go from screen to lens.\n38\t- **Provably no exfiltration** — a static page with no network calls can be\n39\t  audited once and trusted thereafter.\n40\t\n41\t## The hard part\n42\t\n43\tThe channel is **strictly one-way**. The sender has no idea how the receiver is\n44\tdoing — there is no ACK, no retransmit request, no back-channel of any kind. The\n45\treceiver *will* miss frames: autofocus hunting, motion blur, glare, the user\n46\tlooking away.\n47\t\n48\tA naive \"loop through chunks 1..N forever\" transfer degrades badly under loss\n49\t(the coupon-collector problem — the last few chunks take agonizingly long).\n50\tscreenferry's design centers on **rateless erasure coding**: the sender emits an\n51\tendless stream of encoded frames, and the receiver reconstructs the file once it\n52\thas collected *any* sufficient subset. Miss a frame and it simply doesn't\n53\tmatter — the next one is just as useful.\n54\t\n55\t## Status\n56\t\n57\t**Research complete. Phase 1 core codec built (22 tests green). Phase 0 harness and Phase 0.5 spike both partial** — see [`docs/plan/plan.md`](docs/plan/plan.md) §17.2.\n58\t\n59\t- [`docs/plan/plan.md`](docs/plan/plan.md) — the complete application plan\n60\t- [`docs/notes/`](docs/notes/) — design decisions and constraints specific to screenferry\n61\t- [`docs/research/`](docs/research/) — findings:\n62\t  - `qr-encoding-capacity.md` — QR versions, EC levels, bytes per frame, JS encoders\n63\t  - `browser-qr-scanning.md` — camera capture, decoder libraries, binary safety\n64\t  - `fountain-codes-and-protocol.md` — erasure coding for a one-way channel, wire format\n65\t  - `beyond-qr-optical-channels.md` — color barcodes, screen-camera research, what beats QR\n66\t  - `custom-codec-engineering.md` — feasibility of a purpose-built codec in a browser\n67\t  - `pwa-platform-and-ux.md` — offline PWA, file I/O, iOS constraints, UX, testing\n68\t\n69\t## Expectations\n70\t\n71\tThis is not a fast pipe. Realistic throughput is on the order of **kilobytes per\n72\tsecond** — good for keys, configs, documents, and small archives; not for video.\n73\tThe app is designed to be honest about this up front rather than let a user start\n74\ta transfer that would take an hour.\n75\t\n76\t## License\n77\t\n78\tMIT\n79\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":"call_3283c322ae1f494c9e6d4021","session_id":"41d46935-e3eb-4382-bbe3-b55e47b7324a","uuid":"c2f18e1b-d327-409a-b18c-3f5988a83ae4","timestamp":"2026-08-02T19:48:30.680Z","subagent_type":"Explore","task_description":"Explore test structure and zxing usage"}
